transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jared Morales (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO, AtlasHealth), Sana Patel (Platform Eng), Diego Rivera (Security), Lina Gomez (DevOps)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in covering last week's agent upgrade test, KV cache perf, networking flakiness and next steps.

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about 60 minutes on the calendar, quick roll call?
00:05 Marcus Lee: Marcus here, Sana here, Diego, Lina too.
00:08 Alex Chen: Great, Alex and Priya and Jared from Redwood. Cool. Agenda - quick results review, any blockers, then next steps.
00:20 Priya Kapoor: Quick note, we ran the 2.1.0 agent upgrade on the staging cluster last Thursday, there were two minor issues: one, the on-prem manager default route lost a secondary route on restart, and two - we saw a small perf regression in KV cache when sequences went beyond 2k tokens. It's subtle but reproducible.
00:45 Sana Patel: Right, on our end we saw that too; the latency tail went up about 10-15% for long prompts, short prompts were fine. The logs show more frequent cache misses, some entries marked as evicted earlier. Could be the cache TTL or the eviction policy.
01:10 Jared Morales: Just to clarify, when you say "KV cache" are we talking prefix caching in the Redwood runtime or a separate in-memory layer on your side?
01:20 Marcus Lee: We're seeing it on the Redwood agent side - the agent's local cache. I think Lina's setup has smaller RAM than prod.
01:30 Lina Gomez: Yeah, this is a 32GB node in staging. Prod will be 128GB.
01:35 Priya Kapoor: Ok that explains part of it. The agent 2.1.0 has slightly different memory accounting due to a change in the attention cache serialization, so on smaller nodes it can increase eviction rate. We'll push a recommended config for small nodes.
01:55 Diego Rivera: From security - any change to KMS usage with 2.1.0? We can't have keys rewrapped automatically without approvals.
02:05 Priya Kapoor: No automated rewrap; key usage is identical. There is an optional flag to rotate cache encryption keys but it's off by default. We'll document it.
02:20 Alex Chen: On networking - Sana, you had mentioned some flakiness with cross-account peering and route propagation?
02:28 Sana Patel: Yes, intermittently traffic to the private control plane would fail for a few minutes. From our side route tables looked fine, but we noticed that sometimes the peering connection resets when we hit a NAT gateway threshold.
02:45 Alex Chen: Hmm, we have seen similar with AWS when the peering doesn't carry certain metadata - sometimes the health checks get dropped during rekey. Do you have CloudWatch logs around the time?
02:56 Lina Gomez: I attached CloudWatch snapshots to the shared doc - there's a spike around 2026-04-15T03:12Z.
03:10 Priya Kapoor: Thanks, we'll take a look. One mitigation is to put the control plane in the same account or set up a dedicated transit gateway. We'll add recommended patterns to the runbook.
03:30 Marcus Lee: For compliance we prefer cross-account peering vs shared account, but if transit gateway reduces flakiness that might be ok. Need to weigh cost.
03:42 Alex Chen: Totally. We'll include an approximate cost delta in the follow-up.
03:50 Jared Morales: Quick note on routing: our smart routing layer can fallback to hosted endpoints if private control plane is unreachable, but that requires an explicit policy and TLS proofs. We can demo that later if helpful.
04:05 Marcus Lee: We want least-privilege - fallback only for non-PHI workloads.
04:12 Priya Kapoor: Makes sense, we can scope the routing policy by route and model.
04:20 Sana Patel: Back to the KV perf - what configs should we tune? Cache size and TTL? Anything on worker/concurrency?
04:30 Priya Kapoor: First pass: bump agent memory to at least 64GB for the redis-llike cache, increase cache_size to 1.5x, and set TTL to 48 hours for the POC. Also we'll reduce batch concurrency slightly to avoid thrashing. We'll provide a config diff.
04:55 Alex Chen: Can you run a controlled perf run to validate? Maybe use the eval set you shared last week.
05:02 Sana Patel: Yes, we'll re-run with larger nodes and the new config. Expect results by next Tuesday.
05:10 Priya Kapoor: Also, we discovered a small serialization bug that mislabels attention KV keys in some mixed-precision paths - that's in our backlog and a patch is ready; we'll include it in the upcoming agent 2.1.1 which is non-breaking.
05:30 Marcus Lee: Good. Any security concerns with that patch? Diego?
05:36 Diego Rivera: We'll review the patch diff but looks like runtime-only changes. As long as there's no key material change, ok. Please include a signed SBOM.
05:48 Alex Chen: We'll attach SBOM and release notes.
05:55 Priya Kapoor: Scheduling - we want a maintenance window for the on-prem agent upgrade and config change. Propose week of 2026-05-04, two hours per cluster.
06:10 Marcus Lee: Week of 5/4 works for us, prefer evenings PST.
06:18 Alex Chen: Great, Priya will propose times.
06:23 Jared Morales: One more item - we saw a failed request routing when using the customer-internal proxy (squid) that strips certain HTTP headers. If you have a proxy in path we need to whitelist the Redwood headers (x-rd-owner, x-rd-trace).
06:40 Lina Gomez: Noted, we'll check and whitelist.
06:48 Alex Chen: Awesome. Quick recap of action items - Alex to send runbook & upgrade checklist, Priya to draft rollout plan, Sana to run perf tests, Diego to confirm KMS choices. Any other blockers?
07:05 Marcus Lee: None from me. Thanks everyone.
07:10 Alex Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up by Friday with docs.
07:15 (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript may have minor mis-attributions; the term "KV cache" sometimes appears as "kayvee cache" in transcriber. References: shared runbook (link: https://redwood.ai/runbooks/atlas-pilot), cloudwatch snapshots in shared drive (link: drive/atlas/cloudwatch-2026-04-15), perf spreadsheet (link: sheets/atlas-perf-2026).
